acceptedTrade.what: A name far longer than any in use makes a very tall row: a 2,000-character name gives a heading 720 to 2,680 px tall depending on the width, and the row with it.
acceptedTrade.why: The architect settled this and asked that the reasoning be recorded rather than left as his say-so. The longest name in use anywhere today is 64 characters, which is the size the spec names and the size the row is built for; at that size the heading takes two lines. The alternative is a clamp, and a clamp reintroduces exactly what this issue removes — text cut off where a person cannot read it — and would fail the unclipped guarantee the acceptance rests on. So an absurd name buys an absurd row and no name a person would type does. Measured here: 64 characters gives a heading of 370 x 40 at 1280 and 530 x 40 at 1440, two lines, with the directory at its 192 px floor beside it.
